findings.finding: The new ComparableUtils.compare overloads preserve the Comparable<? super T> bound, return compareTo results unchanged for non-null values, and implement the requested null ordering. The default overload passes nullGreater=false; the flag affects only null comparisons and two nulls compare equal.
evidence: Fresh public replay code-kb lookup/context shows ComparableUtils.compare signatures at src/main/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/compare/ComparableUtils.java:163-165 and 178-189 with Comparable<? super T> bounds.
The bodies delegate default ordering to the boolean overload, return 0 for identical references, branch only for null operands, and otherwise return c1.compareTo(c2).

findings.finding: The new varargs max/min return null for null, empty, or all-null input, ignore null entries, and retain the first equal value. Existing two-value overloads keep their previous tie behavior, returning the second equal argument. ObjectUtils compatibility methods retain their signatures and delegate to ComparableUtils.
evidence: Fresh public replay code-kb contexts show ComparableUtils.max/min varargs methods at src/main/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/compare/ComparableUtils.java:273-284 and 311-322 using strict greater-than/less-than updates, while the old two-value overloads remain present at 261-263 and 299-301.

A fresh baseline replay of the frozen seed showed the old two-value max/min used the same strict branch and selected the second argument on ties; the captured patch keeps that branch and routes the comparison through ComparableUtils.compare.

Fresh public replay code-kb contexts show ObjectUtils.compare, max, and min wrappers at src/main/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/ObjectUtils.java:294-296, 312-314, 1022-1025, and 1084-1087 delegating to ComparableUtils.
Code-kb callers reports show the ObjectUtils compatibility methods and the added test class call the ComparableUtils methods.

findings.finding: The added migration test covers both null-ordering modes, the compatibility wrappers, null/empty/all-null varargs, null skipping, first-equal retention, existing two-value behavior, and comparison to a supertype. The trusted grade did not select this new test file, so it was run separately on the fresh public replay.
evidence: Code-kb bodies for all six tests in src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/compare/ComparableUtilsMigrationTest.java show the stated cases, including LocalDate implementing Comparable to a supertype.
The frozen public grade selected ComparableUtilsTest and ObjectUtilsTest; the hidden grade selected ComparableUtilsMigrationContractTest, neither of which selected ComparableUtilsMigrationTest.
The trusted public grade passed 130 tests and the trusted hidden contract grade passed 5 tests.
An offline focused Maven run passed all 6 ComparableUtilsMigrationTest tests on the fresh public replay.
